extra.reason:
Landed. torcl f373a73e (the gate, runtime API 3) and bliss 2a4b171 (EditText through it).

Verified on a Pixel 10 Pro XL, Android 16: mServedInputConnection is an
EditableInputConnection rather than the fallback, isAcceptingText is T, 'hello'
arrives with ZERO key events, and an emoji arrives as one character (U+1F61E)
and renders.

Two things learned that were not in the plan:

* A jobject returned from a main-thread visit is a LOCAL reference belonging to
  MessageQueue.nativePollOnce's JNI frame, and that frame is popped when the
  looper returns to Java. Promoting it on the next visit aborts the process
  (CheckJNI: 'invalid local reference, popped reference at index 11 in a table
  of size 7'). The gate therefore takes optional promote/release functions,
  supplied by the caller, applied before the visit ends.
* Java strings are MODIFIED UTF-8, and neither direction was handling it. Now
  in bliss src/utf8.lisp with 9 desktop checks.

24a51cc. :BOX now stacks its children when it has any and stays a plain rectangle when it does not.

12 new checks (170 total), and verified on a Pixel 10 Pro XL: the panel that
drew nothing now draws, and a badge sits over the corner of another panel --
which no arrangement of rows and columns can produce.

One thing the tests caught that the design did not anticipate: a box with a size
of its own hands that size down as a MAXIMUM, so a child asking for more is
clamped rather than overflowing. The alignment slack is therefore never negative
by construction, and the max-0 guard is belt and braces.

25e60c7. TEXT-FIELD, plus FOCUS-TEXT-FIELD / BLUR-TEXT-FIELD / PUMP-TEXT-INPUT behind a *TEXT-INPUT* plist that IME.LISP installs and that is NIL on a desktop.

15 new checks against a stub editor (185 total), and verified on the device with
a TWO-field form, because one field cannot show the bug seeding prevents: typed
Ada into Name, tapped City, typed Lon, got name="Ada" city="Lon".

25b6111. :ELEVATION emits a (:shadow x y w h radius blur dy colour) op before the fill.

Canvas gets a real Gaussian through a BlurMaskFilter cached per radius;
everything that only fills rectangles -- the software rasterizer and GLES
through FLATTEN-TO-RECTS -- gets concentric low-alpha rings instead, which
accumulate under source-over into a readable falloff.

13 new checks, and measured on the device rather than eyeballed: the pixel below
a raised card is (12,19,25) against a (16,24,32) background and back to
background 20px down. A black shadow on a dark theme is precisely the case where
looking at a screenshot proves nothing.

CARD landed with it, six lines, no new primitive underneath.
The card and its divider both stretch on the device. 7 new checks, 205 total.

8d60e57. WITH-LOCAL-REFS (PushLocalFrame/PopLocalFrame) now wraps every per-frame and per-keystroke JNI path.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to this bead's own premise. It claimed leaked local refs
'overflow the table and abort'. Measured on a Pixel 10 Pro XL, Android 16, that
is false: 1,000 / 50,000 / 250,000 unframed object-returning calls all survived
with the process healthy. 512 is the minimum the JNI SPEC obliges an
implementation to guarantee, not ART's limit -- ART grows the table.

What it does cost, also measured: 200,000 leaked references moved the process
from 118,957 KB PSS to 128,052 KB. About 45 bytes each, plus each one pins the
Java object it names.

So: real leak, right fix, wrong severity. Unbounded growth and uncollectable
objects, not a crash.

41105b7. :PATH primitive with a nonzero-winding scanline fill, reducing to spans so every rect-only backend gets it; Canvas draws it through Skia with a Path cached per command list.

Twelve icons, COMPUTED from two functions (a thick line is four corners either side of a segment; a circle is four cubics at 0.5523) rather than transcribed -- compose-multiplatform-core does not contain material-icons, they are published separately, so there was no geometry to read and guessing artwork from memory produces shapes that look nearly right.

13 new checks, 218 total. All twelve drawn on a Pixel 10 Pro XL with the ring hollow and the circle solid.

Carousels work. SCROLL and VIRTUAL-LIST take :AXIS; VISIBLE-RANGE was already one-dimensional and only its parameter name (ITEM-HEIGHT -> ITEM-SIZE) was vertical.

The bead's premise was incomplete in a useful way: the LAYOUT already offset along whichever axis its stack ran, and the host already delivered both drag deltas, so almost nothing was missing. What WAS missing and not mentioned: SCROLL-BY clamped against the frame's rect-height whatever the axis. A horizontal scroller would have allowed 480 where 400 is correct and run off its own end. There is a test on that number.

10 new checks, 228 total. On a Pixel 10 Pro XL: a 5,000-card carousel of which about eight are ever built, dragged 0-4 to 4-8 and back, and it stops at zero rather than going negative.

Landed 6e66c64, CORRECT and it buys nothing on Canvas. Do not retry it there.

Verified on the desktop: 7 checks, including that a damaged redraw is
pixel-identical to a full one. Kept, because the software rasterizer's cost IS
per-pixel and it genuinely helps there.

On the phone it is flat, across three measurements:

  dragging the carousel   damage  8-18%   present ~32ms   (unclipped 28-42ms)
  typing in a text field  damage 12-23%   present ~33ms
  CLIPPED TO ONE PIXEL    damage      0   present 30-45ms

That last one is the answer. Drawing NOTHING costs the same as drawing
everything, so present's cost is not the drawing. It is issuing ~100 operations
through JNI -- each of which is three to six calls at ~35us plus argument
marshalling -- and a clip removes none of that.

Note the apparent contradiction with the earlier measurement that turning
shadows OFF took present from 42ms to 20-34ms. Both are true: the blur is
genuinely expensive AND the clip does not avoid it, which says Skia computes a
BlurMaskFilter's mask before the clip rejects it. Removing the op helps; clipping
it does not.

So present is bounded by the NUMBER of operations and by blur, not by area.
Follow-ups: bliss-<batching> and caching a blurred shadow as a bitmap.
